problem_statement:
project argument works differently with the --web flag
### Describe the bug
Without the `--web` mode, passing the project name in the project flag, works properly.
However, using the `--web` mode, we need to pass the project path, because GitHub takes the project path as the query parameter
Version of gh: master

### Example
Suppose I have a project named "My Project" in my repo, "testingCLI"
For the non-web version, this works:
`gh issue create -t Title -b Body -p "My Project"`
For the web version, I need to change it to:
`gh issue create -t Title -b Body -p "AliabbasMerchant/testingCLI/1" --web`

### Possible Solution
Either:  
1. We accept the project name everywhere, and convert the name to the path in the web mode (This may cause conflicts when the org and the repo has projects with the same name; But is not a breaking change)
2. We accept the project path everywhere, and convert the path to the name in the normal mode (This may be a breaking change for our users, but will help determine the project much more specifically)
